title: The Afternoon Brief: Domestic terror, settlement expansion, canal cuts shape the day
dek: A foiled Capitol plot, criminal charges escalating against a former congressman, Russia's renewed assault on Ukrainian infrastructure, Israel's settlement acceleration, and a critical global shipping chokepoint narrowing, the day consolidates crises across security, governance, and commerce.
author: GoCheckMyNews
key_fact: An Albany woman was apprehended with an explosive device intended for the New York State Capitol; federal agents escalated their criminal probe of former Rep. Swalwell by seizing his devices; Russia struck Kyiv's critical infrastructure overnight, killing at least 17; Israel opened construction tenders for 1,234 West Bank settlement homes and re-established a settlement evacuated 21 years ago; five Western democracies condemned the move; and the Panama Canal cut daily traffic capacity by 11 percent due to El Niño-driven drought.
bottom_line: An apprehended terror suspect, a criminal probe escalating against a former congressman, Russia's renewed assault on Ukrainian infrastructure, Israel's settlement acceleration despite five-nation condemnation, and a global shipping chokepoint narrowing converge to shape the day. Each represents a stage in a live proceeding: federal investigations with no announced timeline, a war with no negotiated end, territorial expansion tied to October elections, and a weather-dependent canal cut. Watch the West Bank tender deadline on October 19 and the Israeli election on October 27; the NTSB's findings on the Alaska crash; Central American rainfall tracking relative to the Panama Canal baseline; and whether the Swalwell investigation or Bowie proceedings move to charging decisions or trial.
body: The day's picture is one of simultaneous pressure across four distinct theaters: domestic security, congressional accountability, the Ukraine war, and the Middle East. Each represents a stage in a longer process, investigations, enforcement, military escalation, and territorial consolidation, none yet resolved.

On the domestic front, Jessica Bowie, 35, of Albany, was apprehended on August 19 as she gained possession of what she believed to be an explosive device, according to the U.S. Department of Justice. She faces federal charges of attempting to provide material support to ISIS and plotting to deploy that device at the New York State Capitol with intent to kill public officials and "destroy as much of the building as possible" before fleeing to Syria. The investigation involved the FBI, U.S. Secret Service, New York State Police, and Albany Police Department, using confidential sources and surveillance. Simultaneously, federal agents have escalated a criminal investigation into former Democratic Rep. Eric Swalwell by seizing an iPhone and MacBook Pro from his residence in Washington, D.C., and from his arrival at San Francisco International Airport, according to a court filing in the Northern District of California. Swalwell resigned from Congress in April following a House Ethics Committee inquiry into sexual misconduct allegations; investigators are now examining potential federal charges under a statute making it a crime for officials to deprive individuals of constitutional rights. Neither investigation has announced an expected timeline for further proceedings.

In Ukraine, Russian missiles and drones struck Kyiv around midnight, killing at least 17 people and injuring more than 40, according to the Ukrainian State Emergency Service as reported by BBC News. Apartment blocks, warehouses, a children's hospital, and a school were hit; power was cut to thousands of properties. The Ukrainian Air Force indicated that none of the Russian ballistic missiles used in the overnight attack were intercepted, per BBC reporting. The strike marks the first time in several months that critical infrastructure in the capital was purposefully targeted, according to Kyiv's mayor Vitali Klitschko. It compounds Ukraine's winter vulnerability as Russia targets heat and power systems.

In the West Bank, Israel opened construction tenders on Thursday for approximately 1,234 settlement homes in the E1 area, with the deadline falling on October 19, days before Israel's general election scheduled for October 27. The tender covers roughly 12 square kilometers between East Jerusalem and the settlement of Maale Adumim. On the same day, Israel settled 30 "pioneer families" at the Kadim settlement, reversing a 20-year closure and completing the reversal of all four settlements evacuated during Israel's 2005 Disengagement Plan. The UK, France, Germany, Italy, and Canada issued a joint statement calling the tender "unacceptable" and urging immediate withdrawal. The reestablishment of Kadim reflects a broader acceleration under the current Israeli government, which took power in late 2022 and has since overturned the ban on Jewish settlements around Jenin.

Global shipping faces additional constraint: the Panama Canal Authority announced Thursday that it will reduce daily vessel traffic from 36 to 32 ships starting September 15, citing low rainfall caused by El Niño. The reduction affects one of the world's most critical trade chokepoints at a moment when shipping already faces disruptions from conflict in the Middle East.

On the margins, the NTSB is investigating a twin-engine Cessna 441 chartered by the Army Corps of Engineers that crashed at Cape Newenham Long Range Radar Site Airport in western Alaska on Thursday at 12:15 p.m. local time, killing all eight people aboard, two pilots and six passengers. The cause remains under investigation. Federal Judge Nusrat Choudhury ruled on August 21 that former Abercrombie & Fitch CEO Mike Jeffries is competent to stand trial on sex trafficking charges, reversing an earlier incompetency finding; trial is scheduled to begin October 26. The Federal Reserve issued a Written Agreement with SouthPoint Bancshares, Inc., on August 20 and terminated a Cease and Desist Order against Deutsche Bank AG that had been in place since April 2017. Laken Snelling, 22, a former University of Kentucky STUNT team member, pleaded guilty Friday to first-degree manslaughter in the death of her newborn son; sentencing details have not been announced.

What binds these developments is their intermediate stage in longer proceedings. The terror and misconduct investigations are active; the Ukraine war continues; the West Bank settlements face a court challenge and October electoral politics; the Panama Canal capacity cut depends on Central American rainfall. None is finished. All move toward decision points in the coming weeks.
